title: Sod Installation or Irrigation First? Sequencing a Spring Lawn Project
meta_title: Sod or Irrigation First? Sequencing a Spring Project
meta_description: If you're planning both sod and irrigation for spring, the order you install them in matters. Here's the general logic behind sequencing the two.
lede: If a new lawn and a new irrigation system are both on your spring list, the order you tackle them in isn't arbitrary.
excerpt: Why irrigation typically goes in before sod, not after, on a combined project.

sections.heading: Why Irrigation Usually Comes First
paragraphs: Installing irrigation lines involves digging trenches across the yard, which is far simpler to do on bare or prepped ground than it is once new sod is down. Trenching through freshly laid sod risks damaging grass that hasn't even had a chance to establish yet.

sections.heading: What Happens If You Install Sod First
paragraphs: Adding irrigation after sod is already down isn't impossible, but it generally means more disruption to the new lawn, since trenches still need to be dug regardless of what's growing above them. That disruption is exactly what sequencing irrigation first avoids.

sections.heading: Planning Both as One Project
paragraphs: When both are planned together from the start, irrigation placement can also account for where the lawn will actually need coverage, rather than working around grass that's already established. That coordination is easier when both projects are scoped at the same time.

sections.heading: Talking Sequencing Through During a Quote
paragraphs: If you're planning both, it's worth raising the sequencing question directly during your quote conversation so the timeline reflects the right order for your specific yard.

faqs.q: Does irrigation always have to go in before sod?
faqs.a: It's generally the smoother order, since trenching is easier on bare or prepped ground than through newly laid sod.

faqs.q: What if I already have sod and want to add irrigation later?
faqs.a: It's still possible, but it typically means more disruption to the existing lawn since trenches have to be dug regardless.

faqs.q: Should I mention both projects when I get a quote?
faqs.a: Yes. Planning both together lets irrigation placement account for where the lawn will need coverage from the start.
